findings.text: the axis annotation is placed 12,-14 points from the axis inside the contour field, so on all four committed panels the red label text lies across the solved flux contours and the axis marker, which the repository's figure rule refuses to deliver.

the record states the magnetic axis sits at Z between -0.14 and +0.04 m on all four panels, while its own frame-137-diverted-terminal.png labels that axis at Z = -0.44 m, so a reader takes a measured range that omits 0.30 m of the value the figure shows.

the sentence says levels of the opposite sign are dashed, but render_terminal_panels.py:109 passes linestyles=solid and every contour in all four committed PNGs is solid, which is what commit a3cd2debc exists to establish.

_wall_gap duplicates boundary_competition.py:66 _wall_distance, the same roll-clip-project construction over one ring, in a file the node already imports from the same prototype package, so the wall-distance capability now has a second owner.

the committed orchestration script produced none of the geometry the panels consume, since both recorded runs end EXIT_179_LIMITED=1 (geometry_dump.log, AttributeError at record_machine_geometry.py:43; geometry_dump2.log, RuntimeError at :57) and the geometry-limiter-*.npz files the renderer reads were written by a hand command carrying surface=np.zeros((0,2)) and axis=np.zeros(2), so the panels are not reproducible from the tree.
